title: Boss: the site is down at midnight
concept: Rescue the festival site: stash, revert, push

story.speaker: Sam
story.text: The festival site is showing a blank page. The festival opens in nine hours.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Deep breath. Nothing is lost. Let us look at what happened.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: The last commit on main is "Rebuild homepage" and it emptied index.html.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: You also have half-finished work in your folder. Do not throw it away.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Park your unfinished work first, then undo the bad commit, then push the fix.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Undo it with `git revert`, not by deleting history. Other people already pulled that commit.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: When the site is back up, bring your parked work out again.

items.text: Do not lose your draft sponsors page
History was undone safely, not rewritten

hints: Park the draft, undo the bad commit in a way that keeps history, push, then unpark.
`git stash` parks work. `git revert <commit>` undoes a commit by adding a new one. `git stash pop` brings the work back.
`git stash`, then `git revert HEAD` (save the message), then `git push`, then `git stash pop`.
recap: A real rescue: stash the unfinished work, revert the bad commit so history stays honest, push the fix, then pop your work back.

predict.question: Why revert the bad commit instead of deleting it from history?

choices.text: Because teammates already pulled it, so removing it would break their copies
Because revert is faster to type

predict.explanation: Revert adds a new commit that undoes the old one. History stays the same for everyone who already pulled.
